fullPassage:
Living Dictionary

In 1828, an American lawyer and author Noah Webster published "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of providing America with its own version of the English language. Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words should be used rather than documenting the way people actually used English in daily life. In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included informal words in his dictionary, critics accused him of polluting the English language. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations of English, distinguishing American English from British English.

With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations all over the world, for example, with the creation of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes. Now, it is essential for English dictionaries to recognize and document words and phrases that reflect the identities and experiences of the multicultural populations who use English.

questions.passage: In 1828, an American lawyer and author Noah Webster ①<u>published</u> "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of ②<u>providing</u> America with its own version. Most dictionaries in Webster's day ③<u>dictated</u> how English words should be used rather than ④<u>document</u> the way people actually used English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 사전은 사용법을 지시했지 사람들이 실제로 사용하는 방식을 기록하지 않았다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①published: 과거시제, 정상. ✅ ②providing: 전치사 of + 동명사, 정상. ✅ ③dictated: 과거시제, 정상. ❌ ④document: rather than + V-ing 구문에서 documenting 필요. (앞의 dictated와 병렬 시 dictating...rather than documenting 또는 rather than 뒤 동명사)
det.tip: rather than + V-ing: ~보다는. dictated rather than documenting → rather than 뒤 동명사.

questions.passage: In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and ①<u>sought</u> to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included ②<u>informal</u> words in his dictionary, critics ③<u>accused</u> him of polluting the English language. However, Webster argued that these words ④<u>was captured</u> American variations of English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 이 단어들이 미국 영어 변형을 포착했다. these words(복수) + 능동태 captured.
det.analysis: ✅ ①sought: seek의 과거형, 정상. ✅ ②informal: 형용사, 정상. ✅ ③accused: accuse A of B, 정상. ❌ ④was captured: 복수 주어 these words → were 필요하고, captured는 능동(words가 variations를 포착). captured가 맞음.
det.tip: these words captured (능동, O) / these words was captured (X). 단어가 변형을 '포착한' 것.

questions.passage: With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there ①<u>has been</u> a movement to register English variations all over the world. Now, it is essential for English dictionaries ②<u>to recognize</u> and document words and phrases ③<u>that</u> reflect the identities and experiences of the multicultural populations ④<u>whom</u> use English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 영어를 사용하는 다문화 인구. 주격 관계대명사 who 필요.
det.analysis: ✅ ①has been: there has been(현재완료), 정상. ✅ ②to recognize: it is essential to V, 정상. ✅ ③that: 관계대명사 주격, 정상. ❌ ④whom: populations 뒤 관계대명사가 주어 역할 → who 필요. whom은 목적격.
det.tip: who(주격) vs whom(목적격). populations who use English (O) / populations whom use English (X).

questions.passage: In 1828, an American lawyer and author Noah Webster published a dictionary with a goal of ①<u>providing</u> America with its own version. Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words ②<u>should be used</u>. Webster broke this convention and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. These words captured American variations, ③<u>distinguished</u> American English from British English. Now, there has been a movement to register English variations, for example, with ④<u>the creation</u> of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 미국 영어를 영국 영어로부터 구별하면서. 분사구문이므로 distinguishing 필요.
det.analysis: ✅ ①providing: of + V-ing, 정상. ✅ ②should be used: 조동사+수동태, 정상. ❌ ③distinguished: 주절과 동시 동작을 나타내는 분사구문이므로 distinguishing(현재분사) 필요. ✅ ④the creation: 명사, 정상.
det.tip: 분사구문: V-ing(현재분사) = 동시 동작/부가 설명. distinguished는 과거분사로 수동을 뜻하게 됨.

det.korean: 웹스터는 이 단어들이 미국 영어 변형을 포착했다고 주장했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③captured: 변형을 포착. 웹스터의 주장. ❌ ①ignored(무시했다): 반대. ❌ ②rejected(거부했다): 반대. ❌ ④distorted(왜곡했다): 부정적 맥락.
det.tip: capture: 포착하다, 담아내다. 단어가 미국 영어의 특성을 담아냄.

questions.passage: In 1828, Noah Webster published a dictionary with a goal of providing America with its own version. Most dictionaries in his day ①<u>dictated</u> how English words should be used. In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and sought to ②<u>describe</u> the way Americans spoke. When he included informal words, critics ③<u>accused</u> him of polluting the English language. However, Webster ④<u>denied</u> that these words captured American variations.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 웹스터는 이 단어들이 미국 영어 변형을 포착했다고 주장했다(argued). denied(부인했다)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①dictated: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②describe: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③accused: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④denied(부인했다): 원문은 argued(주장했다). 웹스터는 자신의 입장을 주장한 것이지 부인한 것이 아님.
det.tip: argued(주장했다) ↔ denied(부인했다). 웹스터는 비평에 맞서 주장.

questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
